subject: Submission lag impact and evidence bundle for May marketplace billing
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudops.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, finance@cloudops.example.com
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in May AWS Marketplace invoice - possible submission lag

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing a material shortfall on our May AWS Marketplace invoice (~$17.9k) versus our internal usage records. It looks like a number of transactions with timestamps near the 11:59pm UTC cutoff on May 5th weren't processed into the marketplace invoice.

Attached is our export of the usage CSV for May (cloudops_may_usage.csv) with highlighted rows showing submission timestamps between 23:55-00:05 UTC. Can Redwood help validate whether those lines made it into the marketplace ingestion window? If not, we need to submit for retroactive billing.

We'd like to understand the expected timeline for a retrocharge and what evidence AWS will need. Finance is looping in me and our billing mailbox (finance@cloudops.example.com).

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of CloudOps
CloudOps Inc.

Attachment: cloudops_may_usage.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudops.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in May AWS Marketplace invoice - possible submission lag

Hi Elena — thanks for the data and for flagging this so early.

Quick summary of the plan from our side:
- I'll pull our seller submission logs for May 5th and confirm what was accepted by the marketplace ingestion service.
- Jonas will coordinate with Marketplace Support if we have to request a retroactive billing adjustment.
- Vanessa will prepare a consolidated evidence packet (submission logs, signed manifest, and your CSV) for AWS.

I've attached our internal submission log extract for the relevant window (redwood_submission_log_20280510.pdf). Initial look shows several of your rows arrived at 23:58:xx UTC and were accepted, but there are a handful with delayed arrival that may have missed the ingestion window.

Could you also send a PO number or internal reference for the month so finance can match on their side?

I'll keep this thread updated.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa — quick technical note from our ingestion traces:

- For the May 05 23:50–00:10 UTC window we see three failure clusters: transient S3 read spikes (23:56:12), a short replay/duplicate suppression event (23:58:47), and one POST that arrived at 00:06:03 (which is outside the May 05 ingestion cutoff).
- The AWS-side ingestion manifest time is authoritative for what appears on the invoice; anything with final submission after 00:00:00 UTC would fall into the next day's batch.

Recommendation: open a Marketplace Support case requesting retro-billing for items with submission timestamps between 23:55–00:05 UTC where the ultimate ingestion failed/lagged. We should provide: your CSV extract, our submission log, and our internal queueing timestamps.

I'll start drafting the support case language. Vanessa, can you assemble the evidence bundle and confirm the file checksums so AWS can verify?

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hello Karthik / Elena,

Thank you for the evidence. We have opened case AWS-782934 to investigate the May 05 ingestion window.

What AWS needs to proceed:
1) Seller submission manifest (signed or hashed) showing original upload times.
2) Ingestion acceptance receipts or error logs.
3) Customer-provided usage CSV highlighting rows in dispute.

Please upload all items to the secure case portal or provide a signed archive. Once we have the evidence, retro-billing requests typically take 4–8 weeks depending on the volume and whether ledger re-posts are required.

Case reference: AWS-782934

1) Evidence bundle: Vanessa has uploaded a consolidated zip with
   - cloudops_may_usage.csv (customer extract)
   - redwood_submission_log_20280510.pdf (submission/receipt snapshots)
   - checksums.txt (file integrity list)

2) AWS case: AWS confirmed receipt (AWS-782934). Estimated retrocharge window is 4–8 weeks; if ledger re-posts are required we will get a more precise cutoff after the initial review.

4) Next internal steps: Marissa will prepare the accounting memo (journal entry impact) and Jonas will remain on the case until close. Karthik + Vanessa will be primary contacts for AWS.

If OK, Elena — please reply with the PO/ref and confirm we can proceed to submit the signed archive on your behalf to AWS.
